summary: Closed the terminal-write enforcement gap by documenting its scope boundary across three existing source-store markdown files: handoff-schema.md now carries a new 'No Preventive Enforcement of the Terminal Write (Direct-Dispatch Path)' subsection stating that RECOVERY_DECLINED detection is the sole, after-the-fact enforcement on the /orchestrate direct-dispatch path, and skill-lifecycle.md plus system-defect-discrimination.md each carry a one-sentence pointer to it. Deferred the complete gate set to the once-per-invocation batch stage per this dispatch's own '## Batch Gate Deferral' directive, discharging Phase 2's full-tier requirement against the scoped gate subset (--only-gate 3,4) covering the files actually touched.

next_action_hint: Task 428 is fully implemented; no further dispatch needed for this task. The batch-level complete gate run (owed once per invocation) will attribute any finding naming this task's three touched files back to it via modified_files.

user_decision.question: Research found that both fix locations this task names (planner-agent's terminal-write contract and postflight's detection) are already correct and already closed; the only remaining gap is structural -- nothing on the /orchestrate direct-dispatch path can PREVENT a missing terminal write, because no .postflight-pending marker is ever armed for that path. This plan documents that boundary. Should genuine prevention also be funded as a separate follow-up task?
options: Document the scope boundary only (this plan) -- detection via RECOVERY_DECLINED stays the sole enforcement, no new infrastructure
Also scope a separate follow-up task to arm a dispatch-scoped marker in skill-orchestrate and add a SubagentStop-level terminal-status check
